G-F001.trick: Organ = a team of tissues. One tissue alone is just a player, not the team.
G-F001.tip: When an option names only one tissue type, it is too small to be an organ. Look for the answer with several tissues working together.

G-F002.trick: ASSIMilation = ASSEMBLE into you. Absorption only brings it in the door.
G-F002.tip: The stem says "specifically". Pick the most exact process, not a nearby one like absorption or digestion.

G-F003.trick: Breathing runs on a pressure slope: air flows downhill from high to low.
G-F003.tip: Not every survival need is something you eat or drink. Read the stem for the physical condition being described.

G-F004.trick: Negative feedback = "NEGATE the change". The response shrinks the error.
G-F004.tip: To spot negative feedback, ask: does the response push the variable back toward normal? If yes, it is negative.

G-F005.trick: Homeostasis is a thermostat, not a statue: it wobbles inside a safe range.
G-F005.tip: Watch for absolute words like "every" and "perfectly". They usually signal the wrong idea.

G-F006.trick: PERI-cardial = AROUND the heart. The cavity is the thin fluid gap inside the sac.
G-F006.tip: Match the location in the stem to the organ named in the term. Heart → pericardial, lungs → pleural, gut → peritoneal.

G-F007.trick: RETRO = behind. Kidneys hide BEHIND the peritoneum, like a poster behind a curtain.
G-F007.tip: Location words often carry their meaning in the prefix. Break the term apart before choosing.

G-F008.trick: Kidneys MAKE urine; the tubes and bladder only MOVE and STORE it.
G-F008.tip: "Directly forms" points to the organ doing the work, not the system that transports the product.

G-F009.trick: CONTRA = against/opposite (like contrary). IPSI = itself, same side.
G-F009.tip: Paired opposites (ipsi/contra, proximal/distal) are common distractors. Decide same side or opposite side first.

G-F010.trick: Cross-section = slicing a hot dog into coins: across the long axis.
G-F010.tip: For sections of a limb or organ, use the object's own long axis, not the whole body's planes.

C-ch1-organization.trick: ANATOMY = what it looks like (think "a-TOM-y" cuts it open). PHYSIOLOGY = how it works.
C-ch1-organization.tip: Structure vs function: anatomy answers "what and where", physiology answers "how and why".

C-ch1-life.trick: METABOLISM = META (all the) + BOL (changes). Every reaction in the body counts.
C-ch1-life.tip: "All chemical reactions" is the broadest term. Anabolism builds and catabolism breaks down; together they make metabolism.

C-ch1-homeostasis.trick: HOMEO = same, STASIS = standing. "Staying about the same" by constant adjusting.
C-ch1-homeostasis.tip: The key word is "dynamic". Homeostasis keeps values in a range through constant small corrections.

C-ch1-cavities.trick: PARIETAL = the PARTITION (wall). VISCERAL = the VISCERA (organs).
C-ch1-cavities.tip: Serous membranes always come in pairs: parietal on the wall, visceral on the organ, fluid between them.

C-ch1-systems.trick: Cell → tissue → organ → SYSTEM: like player → team → league.
C-ch1-systems.tip: If several organs share one job (e.g., digestion), the answer is an organ system.

C-ch1-directions.trick: Anatomical position: stand tall, look ahead, palms out like you're asking for a hug.
C-ch1-directions.tip: Always describe the body from the patient's anatomical position, even if they are lying down.

C-ch1-planes.trick: SAGITTAL splits you like an arrow (sagitta) shot straight through: left and right.
C-ch1-planes.tip: Sagittal = left/right, frontal (coronal) = front/back, transverse = top/bottom. Picture the cut before choosing.

C-ch1-regions.trick: EPI = above, GASTR = stomach. Epigastric is above the stomach area, right under the ribs in the middle.
C-ch1-regions.tip: Use the patient's right and left for regions. Epigastric (top), umbilical (middle), hypogastric (bottom) run down the center.
